problems.title: Last digit of two powers
problems.question: Find the last digit of 4^(12n+33)+3^(24n+16), n natural.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Powers of 4 alternate4,6; odd exponent gives 4. Powers of 3 have period4.
steps: The second exponent is divisible by 4, so its last digit is 1. Sum ends in5.

problems.title: Largest power of six dividing a factorial
problems.question: Find the largest k for which6ᵏ divides100!.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: Each factor 6 needs one2 and one3, so k=min(97,48)=48.

problems.title: Bisected supplementary angles
problems.question: Two parallel lines cut by a transversal have same-side interior-angle bisectors making acute anglesα,β with the parallels. Their difference is 20°. Find the smaller.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The original angles sum 180°, so α+β=90°.
steps: Together with larger−smaller=20°, this gives smaller=(90−20)/2=35°.

problems.title: Subsets of a set containing sets
problems.question: How many subsets has{a, b,{a},{a, b}, m}?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: A set with n distinct elements has 2ⁿ subsets.
steps: The five listed objects count as five elements, even though two are themselves sets. Thus2⁵=32.
problems.note: The listed objects are assumed distinct, as intended by the question.

problems.title: Integrate an absolute value
problems.question: Evaluate∫₋₂²|x+1|dx.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Split at x=−1, where x+1 changes sign.
steps: The two triangular areas are 1/2 and 9/2. Their sum is 5.

problems.title: Triangles on two parallel lines
problems.question: Eight marked points lie on two parallel lines. Find the maximum number of triangles.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: If k points lie on one line, the count is C(8,3)−C(k,3)−C(8−k,3).
steps: It is maximized by an even split4,4, giving56−4−4=48. Equivalently count 2·C(4,2)·4.

problems.title: A chord ratio in an isosceles cyclic triangle
problems.question: In cyclic ABC, AB=AC. Chord AP meets BC at E, with BE:EC=2:5. Find BP:PC.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: By triangle areas, BE/EC=AB·sin∠BAE/[AC·sin∠EAC]. By equal-circle chord formulas, BP/PC=sin∠BAP/sin∠PAC.
steps: Since E lies on AP and AB=AC, the two ratios are equal.

problems.title: Integrate a cosine square
problems.question: Find∫cos²x dx.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: cos²x=(1+cos2x)/2.
steps: Integrating termwise gives x/2+sin2x/4+C.

problems.title: Ratio of intersecting cevians
problems.question: AN:NC=4:9 and BM:MC=2:7. AM and BN meet at O. Find AO:OM.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Assign masses A=9, C=4, B=14 to match both side ratios. Then mass M=18.
steps: On AM, the division is inverse to endpoint masses:AO/OM=18/9=2.

problems.title: An absolute-value distance equation
problems.question: Count integer roots of|x−2|+|x+4.3|=6.3.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The sum equals the endpoint distance 6.3 exactly when−4.3≤x≤2.
steps: Integers are −4,−3,−2,−1,0,1,2:seven values.

problems.title: Parallel through a trapezoid diagonal intersection
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases a, b. Find the segment parallel to them through the diagonal intersection.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The intersection divides the altitude in the ratio a:b. Parallel section lengths vary linearly with height.
steps: Starting at base a, the length is a+(b−a)a/(a+b)=2ab/(a+b).

problems.title: Difference of supplementary angles
problems.question: One supplementary angle is one quarter of the other. Find their difference.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Let the angles t,4t. Then5t=180°.
steps: They are 36°,144°; difference 108°.

problems.title: Perpendicular bisector in a right triangle
problems.question: K is midpoint of hypotenuse AB; M lies on AC with AM:MC=2:1 and MK⊥AB. Given AC=24, find MK.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: AM=16. Because M lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, MB=MA=16.

problems.title: Angle of intersecting chords
problems.question: The four consecutive arcs cut by two intersecting chords are in ratio1:4:3:10. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: One ratio unit is 360°/18=20°. An interior chord angle is half the sum of opposite intercepted arcs.
steps: The angles are(20+60)/2=40° and its supplement140°. The smaller angle between the lines is 40°.
problems.answer: 40° for the smaller angle; the other angle is 140°.
problems.note: Both 40° and 140° appear among the choices. Without specifying the smaller angle, both are angles formed by the chords.

problems.title: Concentric circles and perpendicular tangents
problems.question: Two perpendicular chords of a large circle touch a concentric small circle. One chord is split into4 and 10 at their intersection. Find the small radius.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Place the tangent lines at x=r, y=r and the common centre at 0. Their intersection is(r, r); the midpoint of the vertical chord is(r,0).
steps: The chord intersection is(10−4)/2=3 from that midpoint. This equals r.

problems.title: Three distinct diagonal lengths
problems.question: A regular n-gon has exactly 3 different diagonal lengths. Which listed n can work?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The number of diagonal lengths is floor(n/2)−1.
steps: Set it equal to 3:floor(n/2)=4, so n=8 or 9. Of9,6,12,10, only 9 works.

problems.title: Divisors avoiding a prime
problems.question: How many divisors of lcm(270,450) are not divisible by 3?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: lcm=2·3³·5². A divisor avoiding3 has form2ᵃ5ᵇ,0≤a≤1,0≤b≤2.
steps: There are(1+1)(2+1)=6 choices.

problems.title: Converse of the secant power theorem
problems.question: Extended sides AB, CD meet at M and MA·MB=MC·MD. What follows?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Equal secant products are the converse of the circle power relation.
steps: The circle through A, B, C meets the second secant at a point whose product with MC is MA·MB. The given equality makes that point D.
problems.answer: ABCD is cyclic:it has a circumcircle.

problems.title: Binary ones in127
problems.question: How many1 digits are in the binary representation of 127?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: Thus its binary for m is 1111111, containing7 ones.

problems.title: Add recurring decimals
problems.question: Compute0.4(8)+0.(2).
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: Their sum is 32/45.

problems.title: Passing a ball around a five-person star
problems.question: Five people stand cyclically:Kamkama, Kvasho, Dona, Tsiskara, Loma. A pass skips neighbours and never returns to the previous passer. Starting with Kamkama, who has the ball after105 passes?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The allowed passing graph is a 5-cycle star. After the first choice, the no-return rule forces continuation around that cycle.
steps: Every5 passes return to the starting person. Since105 is divisible by 5, the ball is with Kamkama.

problems.title: Tangential trapezoid and two midlines
problems.question: A tangential trapezoid has legs3,5. Its midline divides it into trapezoids whose midlines have ratio5:11. Find the base difference.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Let bases a≤b. Tangency gives a+b=8. The two midlines are(3a+b)/4 and(a+3b)/4.
steps: Their ratio gives 11(3a+b)=5(a+3b), hence b=7a. Thus a=1, b=7, difference 6.

problems.title: Which solution set is impossible?
problems.question: Which of empty set,(2,∞),(−∞,0), R cannot be the solution set of ax>a+1?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For a=0, the inequality is false and the set is empty. For a>0, it is x>1+1/a; for a<0, it is x<1+1/a.
steps: The stated half-lines occur for a=1 and a=−1. No value makes the inequality true for every real x.

problems.title: Mix two salt solutions
problems.question: Add how much35% solution to 2 litres of 21% solution to obtain31%?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: Thus0.04v=0.20, so v=5 litres.

problems.title: Prime factors of a power quotient
problems.question: Compute15⁸·75²/(125²·45⁵).
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: The powers of 3 cancel:8+2−10=0. The remaining power of 5 is 8+4−6−5=1.

problems.title: A difference-of-cubes cancellation
problems.question: Simplify(1+2/√a+4/a)²(1−2/√a)² /[(a√a−8)/199]² and evaluate at a=√199.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: (1+t+t²)(1−t)=1−t³, with t=2/√a.
steps: The numerator is[(a√a−8)/(a√a)]². Cancelling gives 199²/a³.
At a=√199, the value is √199.
problems.note: Use a>0 and a√a≠8 for the original quotient; the supplied a is admissible.

problems.title: Containment of open half-lines
problems.question: A solves2x−1<5.8; B solves x−1<m. Find the smallest natural m with A⊆B.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: A=(−∞,3.4), B=(−∞, m+1). Inclusion requires m+1≥3.4.
steps: Thus m≥2.4, and the least natural value is 3.

problems.title: Tangency to a parabola
problems.question: Find all k such that y=kx+3k−7 touches y=x².
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Intersection gives x²−kx−3k+7=0. Tangency requires discriminant0.

problems.title: Remove absolute values using signs
problems.question: For x>y>0, simplify3x−y+√(4x²−4xy+y²)+|3x−y|.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The radical is|2x−y|=2x−y, and|3x−y|=3x−y.
steps: Add the terms to get8x−3y.

problems.title: A sum of nonnegative expressions
problems.question: If(a+4b−6)²+|3a−2b−4|=0, find a+b.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Both terms are nonnegative, so a+4b=6 and 3a−2b=4.
steps: Solving gives b=1, a=2, so a+b=3.

problems.title: Polygon angle sum
problems.question: A convex polygon has interior-angle sum 900°. Find its number of sides.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: Thus n−2=5, n=7.

problems.title: Opposite roots of a parameter quadratic
problems.question: For which a does x²−(a²−16)x+3a+6=0 have equal-magnitude, opposite-sign roots?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The root sum must be0, so a²=16. Their product must be negative.
steps: At a=4, the product 18>0. At a=−4, the product −6<0 and roots are±√6.

problems.title: Midpoint quadrilateral perimeter
problems.question: A convex quadrilateral’s diagonals sum to 18. Find the perimeter of the quadrilateral joining consecutive side midpoints.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Each new side is half a diagonal, by the triangle midsegment theorem.
steps: Each diagonal contributes twice its half-length. The perimeter is the sum of the original diagonals,18.

problems.title: Repeated digit in a product rebus
problems.question: Distinct Georgian letters represent distinct digits in მ·ე·გ·რ·ე·ლ·ა /(დ·ა·რ·ს·ა)=25. Find ე.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Cancel common factors to get მ·ე²·გ·ლ=25·დ·ს·ა. All denominator digits are nonzero.
steps: The right side contains at least two factors 5. Among nonzero decimal digits, only 5 supplies a factor 5. Since distinct letters have distinct digits, the numerator can supply two factors 5 only through the repeated letter ე.

problems.title: Use a given ratio without solving both variables
problems.question: Given(x+y)/y=1/3, find(x+6y)/(x+y).
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
steps: The target is 1+5y/(x+y)=1+15=16.

problems.title: Evenness of a quadratic
problems.question: For which a is(a²−4)x²+(a²−9)x+a²+3a even?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: An even polynomial has zero coefficient on every odd power.
steps: Thus a²−9=0, so a=±3.

problems.title: Angle between a bisector and a cevian
problems.question: K lies on BC,∠BAK=70°,∠AKC=110°, and BM bisects∠ABC. Find the angle between BM and AK.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Since B, K, C are collinear,∠AKB=70°, so triangle ABK is isosceles with AB=BK.
steps: Its angle bisector from B is also the altitude to AK. This is BM, so the lines are perpendicular.

problems.title: Domain of a rational square root
problems.question: Find the domain of √[((2|x|−5)(√2−3))/(x²−7x+10)].
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Because√2−3<0, require(2|x|−5)/[(x−2)(x−5)]≤0, with x≠2,5.
steps: The numerator zeros are −2.5,2.5. A sign chart at −2.5,2,2.5,5 gives the allowed intervals[−2.5,2) and[2.5,5).

problems.title: An inscribed isosceles right triangle
problems.question: A triangle has base30 cm, height 10 cm. An inscribed isosceles right triangle has hypotenuse parallel to the base and right vertex on the base. Find its hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: If the hypotenuse is L, the isosceles-right height to it is L/2. The available parallel width there is 30(1−(L/2)/10).
steps: Set L=30−3L/2, so 5L/2=30 and L=12 cm.
problems.note: The stated inscription is assumed to exist in the given triangle.

problems.title: Equivalent parameter equations
problems.question: Find b for which(1−b)x²+2x−4b=0 and bx²−4x+4b=0 have the same real solution set.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The discriminants are 4+16b−16b² and 16−16b². Both equations have no real roots for b<−1 or b>(1+√2)/2.
steps: For b≠0,1, if the common set had two roots, the coefficient triples would be proportional. The x-coefficient ratio−1/2 is incompatible with both the leading and constant coefficients. A common single double root is also impossible:the second discriminant vanishes only at b=±1.
At b=1, the first equation is 2x−4=0 and the second is(x−2)²=0, so both have exactly root 2. At b=0, the root sets differ.
problems.note: Equivalent equations include the case where both have empty real solution sets. If a nonempty common set were required, only b=1 remains.

problems.title: Messenger along a moving column
problems.question: A5 km column moves at constant speed. A messenger goes from its back to front and back while the column travels12 km. Find messenger distance.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relation, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Let column speed v, messenger speed u>v. Travel time T=5/(u−v)+5/(u+v)=12/v.
steps: With r=u/v, this gives 10r/(r²−1)=12, or 6r²−5r−6=0. The valid root is r=3/2.
Messenger distance=uT=12r=18 km.
problems.note: The messenger is assumed to keep the same speed relative to the ground in both directions.
